target_customer: City commuters buying or subscribing to a tiny EV (price about $9,980 or $200 per month) and enterprise fleet customers
problem: Cars are oversized, costly and polluting for short urban trips.
business_model: Hardware vehicle sales and subscription with swappable batteries

founders.name: Lihang Nong
founders.background_notes: YC bio: working on manufacturing and AI.

technical_complexity.rationale: A new vehicle type requires hardware design, safety certification, manufacturing and battery swapping; very hard for a team of five.

defensibility.rationale: Novel design, but no sourced patents or manufacturing lead; capital needs were the main barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it; sources show no action.

market_need_then: Pre-orders opened June 2022 with a $100 deposit; no number of deposits reported. No pre-launch demand data found.

branding.brand_signature: The Nimbus One tilting pod vehicle design
branding.community_and_virality: Depositors followed on Facebook; later complaints of silence.

brand_strength.rationale: Product got press (TechCrunch, Fortune, InsideEVs) for the design, but no brand identity assets, community or merch evidence; the brand did not drive outcomes.

outcome_analysis: Nimbus built a tilting three-wheel EV prototype, raised $4.7M in seed funding in August 2021 and opened $100 pre-orders in June 2022 targeting 2023 deliveries while seeking a $20M equity and $10M debt Series A. By November 2024 a depositor reported no vehicle seen in over a year and the page out of stock, but the company has not announced a shutdown; the cause is not public and no Series A was found.
notes: YC status Inactive; no official shutdown notice, so exit.type is unknown. Evidence of dormancy is one depositor's blog (2024-11-16) with the author's own speculation about causes, which is not recorded as a factor. Fortune reportedly gave $5.1M total funding (snippet, unverified) vs $4.7M seed from TechCrunch. A Series A was targeted, none found. Competitor lists empty: TechCrunch named none (Gogoro cited only as a battery-swap model). No website listed in directory. Web Archive unreachable.
